analysis:
Both units are head_text excerpts of docs/architecture/inference.md (lines 4074-4930). The only visible patch hunks touch lines 3, 5253-5258 and 5379-5389. These are outside the supplied units: a 'Last updated' date bump, a resident-assistant addition to the resourcePolicySHA256 formula, and a truncated paragraph about the Qwen27 embedded assistant. The supplied excerpts are unchanged context, so I found no behavior change in them and no source or code change. The PR is documentation only.

The context documents bounded authenticated-record transport, with a failed data plane refusing the request and not falling back to raw transport. It also covers per-rank cluster SSD prefix records, whose directory and sealed header name the encoding and which are refused on mismatch. These controls are consistent with T-041 (HMAC-keyed names, encrypted records, a TTL, and the load agreement binding the encoding), and the text introduces no weaker posture. The cluster SSD prefix records are documented as a lossy approximate-restore path, with native mode staying byte-exact. The cluster-tier description does not state its TTL or HMAC-lookup posture. Whether the cluster QwenStagePrefixDiskTier is bound to the T-041 TTL, KEK and salt-scoping mitigations is not verifiable from the supplied text. I treat that as an unverified contract for integration or a later pass, not as a finding.

The patch adds a resident assistant to resourcePolicySHA256, which binds the approval to the declared assistant. This is a tightening, but its patch excerpt is truncated, so the later hunk at 5379-5389 is not visible. The new text points to a Qwen27 resident assistant section that I could not see. No threat-model update is demonstrable from the visible lines.
